A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CCDiff research. The main text and Appendices A-C are readable and matchable, including equations, algorithms, tables, and figures. The shorter v2 reflects layout changes rather than missing scientific material.

before.justification: v1 reports original nuScenes closed-loop simulation results, baseline comparisons, ablations, correlation analysis, and qualitative scenario studies in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulation results, ablations, correlation analysis, and qualitative studies in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The scene encoder, TTC masking, causal ranking, training loss, and combined diffusion guidance remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 standardizes sampling notation and adds a vehicle-dynamics comment without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use nuScenes for the same closed-loop traffic-generation tasks, varying controllable-agent counts and planning horizons. Appendix C retains the same seven urban traffic scenarios.

E2.justification: SimNet, TrafficSim, STRIVE, BITS, and CTG remain the evaluated baselines in the corresponding quantitative comparisons. The appendix also retains the same comparator participation in its qualitative studies.

E3.justification: Both retain the training split, 100 sampled validation scenes, three-second initialization histories, ten-second closed-loop evaluation, and agent-count and planning-period settings. Metrics, preprocessing, model configurations, and training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: The encoder, guidance, and ranking ablations in Tables 3 and 6, causal-feature correlation analysis in Figure 8 and Table 8, and qualitative studies in Appendix C are retained without substantive revisions.

E5.justification: Table 8 retains the same correlation and p-value reporting. Neither version introduces additional repeated-run information, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedures relative to the other.

E6.justification: Tables 1-3, 5-6, and 8 and Figure 4 retain their numerical results, and the appendix retains its qualitative outcomes. For example, CCDiff's full-agent CS and RS in Table 1 remain 0.74 and 0.76.

T1.justification: Definitions 1-2, the mathematical development in Sections 3-4, and Appendix B remain substantively unchanged. Grammar corrections in Definition 2 and notation cleanup in Algorithm 1 do not alter mathematical definitions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: constrained traffic-generation formulation, causal structure-guided diffusion, and improved controllability and realism in closed-loop evaluation.

C2.justification: Interpretations of causal ranking, gradient conflicts, and experimental outcomes are retained. Both conclusions acknowledge dependence on hyperparameter tuning and difficulty directly evaluating the causal reasoning pipeline; appendix edits preserve the existing explanations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-website hyperlink in the abstract. The existing baseline-code link, Table 7 hyperparameters, and hardware and training-time disclosures remain unchanged. The PDFs establish an additional resource pointer but do not establish a new code or data release.

R1.justification: The same 53 references, related-work discussion, and Appendix A comparison table are retained. Bibliographic differences concern citation-page backreferences, with no added works or substantive repositioning.

P1.justification: v2 updates author-name forms, corrects grammar in Definition 2 and Appendix C.5, changes the stray comfort-metric abbreviation CFT to CFD, and adjusts research-question lead-ins and figure references. The section hierarchy and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 compacts the author block, moves Figure 1 onto the first page, repositions Algorithm 1 and Tables 1-3, and removes printed page numbers. Figures and tables retain their substantive displays; the changes are limited layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves presentation through grammar and notation corrections, consistent comfort-metric terminology, and a more compact title-page layout. The added project-site pointer supplies another route to further details. The scientific evidence and stated limitations remain unchanged, so the gains are limited to editorial clarity and access information.
